finding.question: Under current U.S. election rules, are mail-in ballots postmarked before Election Day always rejected if they arrive after Election Day, or do some jurisdictions count them if they arrive within a specified period?
finding.summary: As of October 28, 2020, receipt deadlines varied by state; a timely postmark did not always mean a ballot arriving after Election Day would be rejected. California’s AB 860, signed June 18, required ballots postmarked by November 3 to be counted if received within 17 days afterward; Kansas set a November 6 receipt deadline for ballots postmarked by Election Day. Court decisions also affected deadlines: Wisconsin ballots had to be received by Election Day, while Pennsylvania’s three-day extension remained in place but faced a possible further court challenge.

report_raw.claim: Even if your mail-in ballot is postmarked prior to the Election day but arrives after the Election day it will be thrown out.
report_raw.justification: As of October 28, 2020, some states allowed otherwise valid mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted if they arrived afterward. [S1][S2] California required such ballots to be counted if received within 17 days after Election Day, and Kansas set a November 6 receipt deadline for its November 3 election. [S1][S2] Rules differed by state: Wisconsin required ballots to be received by Election Day. [S3] Inference: The claim is false as a general statement about U.S. elections, although it describes the rule in some jurisdictions.
key_points: California allowed qualifying ballots to arrive up to 17 days after Election Day. [S1]
Kansas allowed qualifying advance ballots to arrive by November 6, three days after Election Day. [S2]
Wisconsin required ballots to be received by Election Day. [S3]
report_raw.counter_argument: The claim accurately described Wisconsin's receipt deadline for the 2020 election: a timely postmark did not save a ballot received after Election Day. [S3] That does not establish a general U.S. rule, because California and Kansas provided later receipt deadlines. [S1][S2]
evidence_gaps: The evidence provides examples rather than a complete state-by-state inventory of deadlines as of October 28, 2020.
Pennsylvania's three-day extension faced possible further judicial review as of the reference date. [S4]
